authorization: Researcher's general thermodynamic-limit proof request; continue the existing autoresearch program.
question: At p=1/2,q=1 on the canonical square, can residual-current geometry establish the L->infinity behavior of the physical logical-sector ratio?
earliest_gate: Review primary literature on random orientations, bond percolation and planar crossing estimates before using an equivalence or critical result.
planned_steps: Derive the residual oriented graph: a zero-current edge can be increased along its arrow, and an occupied edge can be decreased against it. Check whether opposite-sector support is exactly equivalent to a directed path between rough sides.
At the equal-weight midpoint, investigate which random-orientation connectivity results transfer to this exact geometry. Preserve the full physical record distribution.

Identify the missing posterior-balance lemma: a positive probability that both sectors are supported does not by itself lower-bound their smaller normalized weight. Do not equate a percolation crossing with Bayes failure.
Use all 256 directed L3 currents as an exact support/sector-count control. Any larger computation, new geometry or asymptotic lower-bound conjecture requires separate registration.
Deliver a proof, counterexample or sharply stated remaining obstruction; no fitted threshold, decoder sweep or unsupported CFT identification.
priority_update: Researcher explicitly prioritizes decoding transitions and correction thresholds. Bulk-pressure existence and speculative CFT are supporting tools only.
threshold_target: At fixed q define the initial correctable threshold as the supremum of p0 for which every 0<=p<p0 has optimal LER tending to zero. Do not assume monotonicity over the full p interval; p=1 has known activity parity.

primary_sources_reviewed.use: Linusson Lemma 2.1, reproducing McDiarmid: uniform random orientation out-cluster equals p=1/2 bond-percolation cluster in distribution. Prove the seed-set extension explicitly by exploration.
McDiarmid 1981 original provenance; no posterior-sector inference theorem is supplied by this source.
Theorem 4.6 critical bond RSW supplies nonvanishing square-box crossing probability. The removed rough-side vertical edges do not affect the crossing event. No conformal-invariance claim is needed.

registered_finite_controls: All 256 original directed square L3 currents; exact record-sector counts, residual left/right reachability, and support equivalence.
All 256 independent p=1/2 bond configurations on the same L3 graph; compare the complete seed-set cluster distributions, not just crossing probabilities.
Exact ambiguous-record posterior risks and a counterexample, if present, to treating every ambiguous record as an equal-sector tie.
No size extrapolation or inference that the bond threshold 1/2 is a decoding threshold.
decision: Proved residual support and the midpoint seed-set cluster law; RSW establishes nonvanishing ambiguity probability. Exact L3 posterior counts reject equal-sector balance. A size-independent lower bound on physical-record-averaged balance remains necessary for a nonzero limiting LER claim; no square threshold is promoted.
